*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30 IS COMPLETE -- 11 of 11 closed, 10 PASSING (US-555, US-556, US-557, US-558, US-559, US-561, US-563, US-564, US-565, US-566), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560 / BL-034). NO WORK REMAINS IN sprint.json. US-560 is NOT a retry candidate: its premise was refuted by the panel's own EDID (the OSOYOO HDMI35 is a scaler panel and advertises no 480x320 mode at all), so it needs an Atlas ruling + CIO ratify, not another Ralph cycle. PM: the sprint is ready for /sprint-deploy-pm. ***

*** US-559 CLOSED passes:true -- sync stamp now renders `Aug 17, 2026 7:30:28 PM` in LOCAL time from the same 12-hour rule as the top-bar clock; rows/pending moved to the System drill-down. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

**A VERB IN AN AC CAN BE THE WHOLE STORY. 'MOVES to #sys-detail' IS A CLAIM ABOUT REACHABILITY.** The drill-down lists ISSUE rows only (US-509 floor: a green source in a fault list is a fabricated fault) and `tappable` was gated on that list being non-empty -- so dropping the counts there sends them somewhere a HEALTHY sync can never open. Every AC would have read as met while the counts vanished in the common case, and `pending` can be non-zero while the tile is still `ok` (only `stale` drives amber), so 'is my drive backed up' would have become unanswerable. **Generalise: when a story says a fact MOVES, the destination's OPEN condition is part of the acceptance -- check who can reach the new home before you build the move.**

**WIDEN AN INVARIANT'S INPUT, NEVER THE INVARIANT.** US-509's rule is 'tappable only when there is SOMETHING behind it' -- not 'only when something is BROKEN'. The CIO's placement call put content behind it in the healthy case, so the rule is untouched and its input changed. Say which one you moved, in the code and in the test, or the next reader reads it as a guard being relaxed.

**SPLIT A COMPOUND PIN WHEN ITS SUBJECT MOVES -- DON'T INVERT IT.** `allGood -> tappable is False AND rows == []` became THREE tests: healthy lists no issue rows / healthy is reachable for diagnostics / neither-rows-nor-diagnostics is NOT tappable. Without that last one the widened gate could be hard-coded `true` and everything else stays green.

**`new Date` IS TOO WILLING -- isNaN IS NOT THE WHOLE GUARD.** `new Date("412")` is the year 412, and a ZONELESS ISO string is read as LOCAL. Neither is an Invalid Date, so both sail past a literal isNaN check and paint a confident wrong date -- and the zoneless case lands silently hours off, re-creating the very contradiction the story removes. Accept only a zone-qualified ISO-8601 instant by pattern; echo everything else verbatim. **The AC said 'never 1970/NaN'; the fabrications that actually reach the glass are the ones that parse SUCCESSFULLY.**

**A TIMEZONE ASSERTION IS VACUOUS ON A UTC RUNNER.** Comparing node's output to Python's `astimezone()` proves local-vs-UTC only on a machine that isn't UTC. Pair it with a STRUCTURAL pin (`getUTCHours` not in the function body) that holds everywhere. This runner is UTC-5 (`11:00:00Z` -> `6:00:00 AM`), so all of it bites here -- but CI might not be.

**RE-POINT YOUR OWN LAST ITERATION'S PINS, ESPECIALLY THEN.** US-564's five null-honesty assertions read `tile["detail"]`, which no longer carries the counts. Re-pointed to `tile["counts"]` with a header note. Deleting a guard because its FIELD was renamed is easiest to justify when you wrote it yesterday.

**COUNT A RULE WITH COMMENTS STRIPPED.** 'The 12-hour rule appears exactly once' is inflated by every comment that quotes the rule -- and this codebase comments heavily. Strip first, then count; and pair the count with a delegation check, because a count of 1 is also satisfied by deleting the other caller.

**ANSWER BL-034 EXPLICITLY EVEN WHEN IT DOESN'T BITE.** It cannot invalidate US-559: the change is a string format, and the new stamp is strictly SHORTER than the one it replaces (23 chars vs 47), so no band budget is worse off than before the commit. One line, much stronger than silence.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs for python -- Write a temp .py and run it. `git commit -m @'...'@` (single-quoted here-string, closing delimiter at column 0) DOES work. **pytest prints NO summary line in this repo's config** -- gate on `$LASTEXITCODE` plus 'zero F/E characters in the progress output'. tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 948 tests, ~4-5 min -- run it FOREGROUND (TD-059), and it IS the right fence for any specs/UI/dist/** change (US-540-b). `carousel_probe.js` is variadic: `_probe(fn, *args)` JSON-encodes each. Index lock CLEAR all session.

If you touch dashboard.css within ~1800 chars of that selector, do not write a bare hash in a comment.
